instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and line two sheet pans with parchment.
Cut the eggplants into 1/2-inch rounds. Toss them on the pans with 1/4 cup of the oil and 1 tsp salt, and spread them in a single layer.
Roast for 18 minutes, flipping them once halfway, until they're soft and golden at the edges.
Meanwhile, slice the garlic. Heat the remaining 1/4 cup oil in a wide pan over medium. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes, until fragrant and not browned.
Add the tomatoes, basil sprigs, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper. Fill the empty can halfway with water and add that too. Simmer for 15 minutes, until it's thickened.
Take out the basil. Stir in the sugar and balsamic vinegar.
Overlap the roasted eggplant in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Pour the sauce over it, then crumble the feta on top.
Bake for 10 minutes, until the sauce is bubbling and the feta is browned in spots.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve warm.
method_notes: Baked eggplant under a garlicky tomato sauce with feta on top is the dish in every version. The lead (Scrummy Lane, 4.91 from 61) bakes halved eggplants for 45 minutes; here they're sliced into rounds and roasted at 425°F, as the second version slices them, so it fits in 45 minutes. That second version fries them, which is left out. The amounts are doubled from the lead, which serves 2 as a main, so 4 can eat it as one.
